question: A 19-year-old South Asian male presents to the family physician concerned that he is beginning to go bald. He is especially troubled because his father and grandfather "went completely bald by the age of 25," and he is willing to try anything to prevent his hair loss. The family physician prescribes a medication that prevents the conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone. Which of the following enzymes is inhibited by this medication?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Testosterone -> Converted to dihydrotestosterone -> Inhibited by medication -> 5-alpha-reductase -> 95%
enhanced_information: The medication prescribed inhibits the conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone by targeting the enzyme 5-alpha-reductase. This aligns with the standard consensus in treating male pattern baldness. The evidence path showing the interaction between testosterone and Stanolone supports the role of 5-alpha-reductase inhibition in this process.
analysis: Male pattern baldness is commonly associated with the conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone. The medication prescribed inhibits this conversion by targeting the enzyme 5-alpha-reductase. This aligns with the standard treatment approach for hair loss in males.
